title: (Hom-inj) for the constructible cocone
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and $X$ a scheme whose underlying topological space is Noetherian. The
constructible cocone ([def-sfb-constructible-cocone]) satisfies (Hom-inj) of
[sk-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit]: if two morphisms $g,g'\colon K\to L$ in
$D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,H)$ satisfy $T_{H,\Qlb}(g)=T_{H,\Qlb}(g')$, then
$T_{H,H'}(g)=T_{H,H'}(g')$ for some finite extension $H'\supseteq H$.

proof.text: Write $R=H_X$ and $S=\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}$, and let $T:D(\operatorname{Mod}_R)\to D(\operatorname{Mod}_S)$ be total left derived scalar extension. By [def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar] and [def-sfb-constructible-extend-to-qlbar], the cocone functor $T_{H,\Qlb}$ is precisely the restriction of $T$, on both objects and arrows. Check the coefficient convention needed below: [def-sfb-padic-subfield-condensed-ring] gives $\underline H(P)=C(P,H)$, while [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed] gives continuous maps into $\Qlb$ whose image is contained in one finite intermediate field. The first is exactly the ring $\underline E(S)=C(S,E)$ of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category] for $E=H$; the second is the finite-subfield-valued continuous-function condensed $\Qlb$ that the statement of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-coefficient-derived-faithful] (step 2) names explicitly, the node [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category] itself defining only finite-field coefficients. The inverse image in [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point] is the same composite $\pi_X^*\circ(\mathrm{sheafify}\circ\operatorname{Lan}_{u^{\mathrm{op}}})$ used there. Thus the rings, inclusion and ambient derived scalar extension agree; this is an unfolding of their definitions, without identifying the finite-subfield-valued coefficient ring with all continuous $\Qlb$-valued functions. Forgetting to the ambient category, the assumed equality is $T(g)=T(g')$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-coefficient-derived-faithful] with $E=H$, $\Omega=\Qlb$ and this scheme $X$. Its hypothesis is any scheme, a prime $\ell$, and a finite intermediate field, all present here; its rings are $p_X^*$ of $C(-,H)$ and of the finite-subfield-valued condensed $\Qlb$, with the same inverse image, as checked in step 1. It says that $T$ is faithful on the entire ambient derived category. Faithfulness means that its map on each Hom set is injective, so $T(g)=T(g')$ implies $g=g'$ in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{H_X})$. By [def-sfb-dcons-subfield], the constructible category is a full subcategory with precisely these ambient morphisms; hence $g=g'$ also in $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,H)$.

Take the finite extension $H'=H$, with its reflexive inclusion. Applying the transition functor $T_{H,H}$ supplied by [def-sfb-constructible-cocone] to the equality $g=g'$ gives $T_{H,H}(g)=T_{H,H}(g')$. This is the eventual-equality assertion (Hom-inj) of [sk-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit]. No identification of $T_{H,H}$ with the identity is needed: every functor maps equal arrows to equal arrows.
